profile.name: Mohammed Javad
profile.summary: Software Developer based in Kochi, India — building fast, expressive web products end-to-end from database schema to polished UI.
intro: I started programming in higher secondary school with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, then built a foundation in C/C++ and core OOP concepts in Java before committing to software development.

That path led through a MERN stack apprenticeship at Devxtra into a software developer role at Bytsolv, where I've gone from learning fundamentals to independently shipping production applications. I enjoy building end-to-end — from database schema to polished UI — and I'm currently expanding into AI-assisted developer tooling and mobile development with React Native.

experiences.description: Independently designed and built roughly 90% of Papr.work v1 — a financial paperwork tracking product for early-stage startups — taking a product concept from database schema and system architecture through to a shipped, live application with React 19, TanStack Router/Query, Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui, Hono, Drizzle ORM, and PostgreSQL. Also contributed full-stack features to SmileOS, a SaaS platform for dental clinics used by 5,000+ practices across Australia, and remain.fit.

projects.name: Papr
projects.description: Financial paperwork, tracked — ledger, invoices, expense tracking, and PDF storage for early-stage startups and small companies without an accountant. Built with React 19, TanStack Router/Query, Hono, Drizzle ORM, and PostgreSQL.

caseStudy.problem: Small companies without an accountant still have to track a ledger, invoices, expenses, salaries, payments and the PDFs behind them. Papr.work is that product: one place for financial paperwork, spanning a web app, a mobile app, an admin portal and employee self-service.
caseStudy.role: Primary engineer on v1 — database design, system architecture, the Hono API, the React 19 web app, the React Native/Expo mobile app, and the admin and employee portals. Delivered roughly 90% of v1 as the sole engineer, merging 24+ pull requests in about a month, all through senior code review.
caseStudy.architecture: A Hono API over PostgreSQL through Drizzle ORM, with Zod request validation and Argon2 password hashing. The React 19 web app and the React Native/Expo mobile app share TypeScript contracts and validation. A Model Context Protocol server with OAuth authorization exposes financial documents, payments, ledger queries and employee self-service to AI clients.
challenges: Closed a security issue by moving document previews into a sandboxed iframe.
Built a reusable terms-template system for invoices and quotations, plus custom document templates.
Implemented a forgot-password flow alongside Argon2-based authentication.
Kept the web and mobile clients on the same TypeScript contracts and validation, so invoices, expenses, salaries and payments render identically on both.
outcomes: Papr.work v1 is live at papr.work.
One backend serves the web app, mobile app, admin portal and employee self-service portals for payslips, payments, profiles and leave requests.
AI clients can work with Papr.work data through the MCP server, authorised with OAuth.
